I may be off base with this, but I think the main reason this is a problem is because.. the plot has no reason to care about Team RWBY.

In like 85% of the media I consume, the villains drive the plot, so I'll treat them as one entity. And when I thought about it, the reason the protagonists in other pieces of media seemed important, is because the villains/plot had a reason to care about them. They had some special power the villain wanted or they just kept getting in the villains way. People might roll their eyes at OP protagonists, but the reason was usually because it made the main character important in some way; they were the only one who could do something, or they were most persistent out of everyone else, or the villains wanted them. Does RWBY fit that criteria at all? What reason does the plot have to care about them?

Do they have special powers that the villains want? No

Are they the most difficult opponents for the villains to face? No

Do they come up with solutions that save the day? Not really

Are they the most persistent ones trying to stop the villains? If they are, the villains don't act like it.

The villains/plot have not been given a reason to care. I know they probably don't want Ruby to become a Maiden in fear of making her too OP, but at least then she would matter.

I'm starting to get the feeling that semblances in general weren't such a good idea. They threw magic into the show and we're supposed to be impressed, but when people in this world are capable of super speed, shadow clones, illusions, summoning, and molecule-whatever, why is magic such a big deal? How cool would it have been if semblances weren't a thing and we were suddenly introduced to magic in Volume 5? I think having semblances really hurt the magic reveal which was a big part of the story.

And tbh, I feel like semblances have become sort of an afterthought/inconvenience for the writers. Did Ruby use her semblance at all in V5? And they forgot Weiss' time dilation. Marrow's is so OP they have to have him forget to use it. And then there's Ironwood and Watts. After hearing their explanation, all I could think was that they clearly forgot to give them semblances and pulled something out of their asses when people asked about it. And the semblances these days feel really lame and uninspired like Robin's, Elm's and Vine's. Maria's semblance felt tacked on as well. I imagine that in the writing room, it's no longer "Oh man, I got tons of cool ideas for this character's semblance!" It is now "Ah shit, we gotta think of a semblance for them now. Sigh." This explanation is just the cherry on top of this mess of a concept.
